---
title: "R and Stata side by side"
description: >
  The arguments of the R function and the options of the Stata command,
  matched, with the few places where the two differ.
---

The R package and the Stata command implement the same procedure and print
the same quantities. This page matches their arguments, options and results,
for readers who move between the two or who want to translate an example.

## The same analysis in both

In R:

```r
out <- bootmakr(y ~ d + x1 + x2, data = dat, treat = "d",
                benchmark_covariates = "x1", kd = c(0.5, 1, 2),
                cluster = "firm", reps = 10000, seed = 123)
out
plot(out, type = "kd_sweep")
```

In Stata:

```stata
bootmakr y d x1 x2, treat(d) benchmark(x1) kd(0.5 1 2) ///
    cluster(firm) reps(10000) seed(123) plot
```

Two things differ by design. The point estimates are identical, but the
bootstrap standard errors, intervals and *p*-values agree only up to
simulation error, because R and Stata have different random-number
generators and the same seed does not give the same bootstrap samples. And
in R the result is an object that you print and plot, whereas in Stata
options of the command request the plot and the diagnostics.

## Specifying the analysis

| Purpose | R | Stata |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `formula = y ~ d + x1 + x2`, `data = dat` | `y d x1 x2` (outcome first) |
| Treatment | `treat = "d"` | `treat(d)` |
| Benchmark covariate | `benchmark_covariates = "x1"` | `benchmark(x1)` |
| Group of covariates as benchmark | `gbenchmark_covariates = c("x1", "x2")` | `gbenchmark(x1 x2)` |
| Strength relative to the benchmark, treatment side | `kd = 1` (default) | `kd(1)` (default) |
| Strength relative to the benchmark, outcome side | `ky`; defaults to `kd` | `ky()`; defaults to `kd()` |
| Several strengths at once | `kd = c(0.5, 1, 2)` | `kd(0.5 1 2)` |
| Categorical covariates | `factor(year)` in the formula | `i.year` in the variable list |
| Subsample | subset `data` | `if` and `in` |
| Regression weights | `weights = "w"` or a vector | not available (`sensemakr` for Stata does not accept weights) |
| Omitted-variable strength set by hand | `r2dz.x`, `r2yz.dx` | not available |

## The bootstrap

| Purpose | R | Stata |
|---|---|---|
| Number of replications | `reps = 1000` (default) | `reps(1000)` (default) |
| Seed | `seed = 123`; none by default | `seed(123)`; none by default |
| Resample observations | no `cluster` | no `cluster()` |
| Resample clusters | `cluster = "firm"` | `cluster(firm)` |
| Two-way clustering | `cluster = c("firm", "year")` | not available |
| Stratified bootstrap | `strata = "region"` | `strata(region)` |
| New cluster identifier in each bootstrap sample | not needed | `idcluster()` |
| Confidence level | `alpha = 0.05` (default) | `alpha(0.05)` or `level(95)` (default) |
| Progress display | `progress = TRUE` (default) | `dots(100)`; off by default |
| Bootstrap your own program | not applicable | `program()` |

## Results, plots and diagnostics

| Purpose | R | Stata |
|---|---|---|
| Table of adjusted estimates | `print(out)`, `out$results` | printed; `r(estimate)`, `r(se)`, `r(ci_lower)`, `r(ci_upper)`, `r(p)`; `r(results)` with several `kd()` |
| Benchmark strength | printed; `out$benchmark_strength` | printed; `r(r2dxj_x)`, `r(r2yxj_dx)`, `r(r2dz_x)`, `r(r2yz_dx)`, `r(benchmark_strength)` |
| Bootstrap draws | `out$boot_samples` | `saving(filename)` |
| Replications completed and failed | `out$N_successful`, `out$N_fail`; note below the table | `r(N_successful)`; warning below the table |
| Plot of the kd sweep | `plot(out, type = "kd_sweep")` | `plot` option |
| Histogram of the bootstrap distribution | `plot(out, type = "histogram")` | top panel of the `converge()` graph |
| Convergence check | `converge = list(minreps = 1000, stepsize = 1000, threshold = 10000)`, then `plot(out, type = "convergence")` | `converge(minreps(1000) stepsize(1000) threshold(10000))` |
| Convergence statistics | `out$convergence` | `r(conv_se_mean)`, `r(conv_p_range)`, ...; `savedata()` inside `converge()` |
| The underlying `sensemakr` result | `out$sensemakr_orig` | run `sensemakr` with the same variables and options |

## Differences worth knowing

**Two-way clustering is available in R only.** With two cluster variables
the R function combines three bootstraps with the estimator of Cameron,
Gelbach, and Miller (2011) and reports normal-approximation intervals
instead of percentile intervals. See
[Clustered and stratified data](clustering.html).

**Weights are available in R only.** The Stata command passes weights on to
`sensemakr`, and the version of `sensemakr` on SSC does not accept them.

**`program()` is specific to Stata.** It bootstraps an e-class program of
your own that calls `sensemakr`. See
[Get started in Stata](stata.html#bootstrapping-your-own-program).

**Five Stata options depend on `sensemakr`.** `kr()`, `r2dxj_x()`,
`r2yxj_dx()`, `bound_label()` and `reduce` are handed to `sensemakr`
unchanged. The version on SSC at the time of writing does not accept them,
so they stop with an error. The help file says so.

**Row labels differ.** With several values of `kd`, R labels the rows
`d (kd=0.5)` and Stata `d_.5`.

## References

Cameron, A. C., Gelbach, J. B., & Miller, D. L. (2011). Robust inference with
multiway clustering. *Journal of Business & Economic Statistics*, 29(2),
238--249. <https://doi.org/10.1198/jbes.2010.07136>
